news.services module

Explicit approval and post-commit integration (brief option 2).

Instead of a signal, the approval view calls approve_article. After the database commit, dispatch_approval emails subscribers and POSTs the approved article to our own /api/approved/ endpoint.

news.services.approve_article(article_id, editor)[source]

Approve an article and schedule notifications after commit.

The article row is locked while it is approved, and the subscriber email and API log are only sent once the transaction commits.

Parameters:

  • article_id (int) – Primary key of the article to approve.

  • editor (news.models.User) – The user approving the article.

Returns:

The approved article.

Return type:

news.models.Article

Raises:

  • django.core.exceptions.PermissionDenied – If editor is not an editor who oversees the article, or wrote it themselves.

  • news.models.Article.DoesNotExist – If no article has that id.

news.services.dispatch_approval(delivery_id)[source]

Email subscribers and log the article to /api/approved/.

Each channel is attempted only if it has not already succeeded. Failures are logged and stored on the delivery so an editor can retry from the article page; they never undo the approval itself.

Parameters:

delivery_id (int) – Primary key of the ApprovalDelivery to process.

Returns:

None. The outcome is saved on the delivery record.

news.services.save_article_changes(article, changes)[source]

Serialise edits with approval and reset review on content changes.

If any field actually changes, the article is unapproved and its revision is incremented, so it disappears from public pages until an editor approves it again.

Parameters:

  • article (news.models.Article) – The article being edited.

  • changes (dict[str, object]) – New values keyed by model field name.

Returns:

The saved (and possibly unapproved) article.

Return type:

news.models.Article

Raises:

django.core.exceptions.ValidationError – If the changes break the article’s author/publisher rules.

news.services.send_newsletter(issue, user)[source]

Email a curated issue, excluding stories returned to draft.

Parameters:

  • issue (news.models.Newsletter) – The newsletter issue to send.

  • user (news.models.User) – The user sending the issue.

Returns:

The number of subscribers the issue was sent to.

Return type:

int

Raises:

  • django.core.exceptions.PermissionDenied – If user cannot manage the issue.

  • ValueError – If the issue has no approved stories.
